title: Social enterprises
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:35Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: Neither bank point teaches social enterprises: the government enterprise card is about government ownership, and the externalities card is about market failure in economics, so the new point needs its own card.

draft.title: Social enterprises
card: A social enterprise is a business that trades to meet a social or environmental purpose. It sells goods or services, as other businesses do.
Most of its profit goes back into that purpose, such as training people or protecting the environment. Little is paid out to owners.
Its main aim is the social or environmental purpose, not profit for owners. It still needs to earn enough to keep trading.
This is different from a charity that relies mainly on donations. A social enterprise earns its income by selling.
draft.remember: A social enterprise sells to earn income, then puts most profit into its purpose.

a.q: Which description best fits a social enterprise?
opts: It sells products and puts most profit into a social purpose
It collects donations and gives all of them to a cause
It sells products and pays most profit to its owners
It is owned by government and sells to make a profit
a.why: A social enterprise earns income by trading and directs most profit to its purpose. A donation-based group is different, because a social enterprise earns its income by selling.
a.clue: Think about how it earns income and where profit goes.

b.q: Tariq opens a bakery in Geelong that employs people who have been out of work for years. Most of its profit pays for more training places. Why is it a social enterprise?
opts: It trades and puts most profit into a social purpose
It employs people, which all businesses do
It makes a profit, so it must serve its owner
It sells bread, which meets a basic need
b.why: The bakery sells goods and puts most profit into training, a social purpose. Making a profit alone does not make a business a social enterprise, because many businesses do that.
b.clue: Look at what happens to the profit.

a.best: It sells products and puts most profit into a social purpose

b.best: It trades and puts most profit into a social purpose
